Alright, the TUI is up and responding to basic commands. I’ve already verified that the `/help` command works and that a bare Enter keypress is processed without issue. The next milestone is to confirm that the live‑agent turn (i.e., when the user types a natural‑language request) correctly triggers the tool‑approval workflow we just fixed.

What does a “live agent turn” look like in this UI? According to the earlier code in `src/tui.tsx`, when the user submits a prompt, the system parses it, potentially calls a tool (e.g., a file‑write tool), and then asks for user approval before actually performing the side effect. The race I just patched was about updating `activeToolHintRef` synchronously, so the approval UI should now show the correct hint immediately.

To test this end‑to‑end, I need a prompt that will invoke a write‑file tool. The simplest is something like “create a file colors.txt with three color names, one per line”. That should cause the agent to plan a `writeFile` tool call, then present an approval request in the UI. I want to see that request appear, and that the system doesn’t crash or hang.

How do I simulate typing that into the TUI? All prior interactions have been done via tmux `send-keys`. The pattern is:

1. `tmux send-keys -t glint "<text>"` – type the prompt.
2. A short sleep (≈0.3 s) to let tmux buffer the characters.
3. `tmux send-keys -t glint Enter` – submit the prompt.
4. A longer sleep (≈8 s) to give the agent time to process, invoke the tool, and display the approval UI.
5. Capture the pane, strip empty lines, and show the last few lines (tail -22) to see the approval prompt and any response.

I’ll follow exactly that pattern, just as I did for the `/help` test. The only difference is the prompt text and the longer wait time because the agent needs to run a model inference and generate a tool request. I’ll also pipe the capture through `grep -v '^$'` to remove blank lines, making the output easier to read.

Thus, the appropriate Bash command is:

```bash
tmux send-keys -t glint "create a file colors.txt with three color names, one per line" && \
sleep 0.3 && \
tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && \
sleep 8 && \
tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^$' | tail -22
```

This will let me verify that the live‑agent turn triggers the approval flow correctly. I'll now execute this as a tool call.
